adams-pearmain.heading: ADAM'S PEARMAIN
adams-pearmain.quality: This is one of the best late dessert sorts
adams-pearmain.climate: it thrives in nearly all soils.
adams-pearmain.note: Synonyms Hanging Pearmain, Norfolk Pippin as in our aka.

allington-pippin.heading: ALLINGTON PIPPIN
allington-pippin.flavour: Flesh, crisp, juicy, pale yellow, sub-acid, pleasantly aromatic.
allington-pippin.quality: A most valuable variety, which is now in the front rank.
allington-pippin.note: Book's synonym: South Lincoln Pippin. Introduced by the author's firm in 1896.

annie-elizabeth.heading: ANNIE ELIZABETH
annie-elizabeth.quality: A valuable fruit deserving of extended cultivation.

antonovka.heading: ANTONOWKA
antonovka.flavour: Flesh, white, loose grained, rather dry, aromatic.
antonovka.quality: This is hardly worthy of retention and is best described as a late edition of White Transparent.
antonovka.note: Described as 'a very popular central Russian variety'.

api.heading: API
api.quality: It is hardly worthy of cultivation except as a curiosity.
api.note: Synonyms Api rouge, Api petit, Lady.

aromatic-russet.heading: AROMATIC RUSSET
aromatic-russet.flavour: Flesh, firm, aromatic, greenish white. A nice winter fruit, of Nonpareil flavour.
aromatic-russet.quality: A nice winter fruit, of Nonpareil flavour.
aromatic-russet.note: Bunyard notes confusion: probably Hogg's Aromatic Russet but not that of Ronalds or Lindley; possibly the Petit Barbaric of Normandy.

arthur-turner.heading: ARTHUR TURNER
arthur-turner.flavour: Flesh, white, slightly acid, baking very well.
arthur-turner.quality: A very handsome apple, which deserves cultivation for an early winter cooking variety.

ashmeads-kernel.heading: ASHMEAD'S KERNEL
ashmeads-kernel.flavour: Flesh, firm, pale yellow, very aromatic.
ashmeads-kernel.quality: A valuable fruit for late use but a poor cropper.
ashmeads-kernel.note: A larger form, Improved Ashmead's Kernel, has its own entry.

red-astrachan.heading: ASTRACHAN RED
red-astrachan.quality: A most attractive fruit but too poor a cropper for general use.
red-astrachan.note: Index line 'Red Astrachan : see Astrachan Red'. Synonyms American Red, Anglesea Pippin.

autumn-pearmain.heading: AUTUMN PEARMAIN
autumn-pearmain.storage: Dessert or culinary, September to October
autumn-pearmain.note: Bunyard: 'It is the Summer Pearmain, of Hogg, but not of Continental Authors.' Mentioned by Parkinson 1629.

barnack-beauty.heading: BARNACK BEAUTY
barnack-beauty.flavour: Flesh, crisp, fair flavour, briskly acid, yellowish.
barnack-beauty.storage: Quite one of the most interesting fruits in February, as it keeps its acid flavour later than many.
barnack-beauty.climate: which does well on chalky sub-soils.
barnack-beauty.note: Season: culinary or dessert, December to March.

beauty-of-bath.heading: BEAUTY OF BATH
beauty-of-bath.flavour: Flesh, tender, yellowish, often stained with red, sweet and pleasant.
beauty-of-bath.quality: This is a very attractive fruit, which is now largely grown for market purposes.

beauty-of-hants.heading: BEAUTY OF HANTS
beauty-of-hants.flavour: Flesh, very crisp, yellowish, highly aromatic.
beauty-of-hants.quality: A fine form of Blenheim Orange.
beauty-of-hants.note: French synonym 'Seedling Offine' (our aka Ofine Seedling). Bunyard insists it is distinct from Blenheim (core and seeds differ).

beauty-of-kent.heading: BEAUTY OF KENT
beauty-of-kent.quality: A very valuable cooking apple for late use.

belle-de-boskoop.heading: BELLE DE BOSKOOP
belle-de-boskoop.flavour: Flesh, firm, yellowish, flavour acid and aromatic.
belle-de-boskoop.quality: A valuable fruit much grown for market in Holland and Germany, and worthy of trial for this purpose in England.
belle-de-boskoop.storage: Culinary or dessert, December to April
belle-de-boskoop.note: Not to be confused with the Calville von Boskoop; Reinette von Montfort considered by some the correct name.

belle-de-pontoise.heading: BELLE DE PONTOISE
belle-de-pontoise.flavour: Flesh, tender, white, sweetish and juicy.
belle-de-pontoise.quality: A very useful variety, keeping firm and acid, but rather tender and best for garden use.
belle-de-pontoise.note: Seedling of Emperor Alexander, raised by M. Remy.

bens-red.heading: BEN'S RED
bens-red.flavour: Flesh, firm, pale yellow, sweet, aromatic.
bens-red.quality: A very useful fruit, valuable for its great cropping qualities.

bess-pool.heading: BESS POOL
bess-pool.storage: A good old sort, keeping firm and crisp to the last.
bess-pool.note: Heading OCR has a stray '^'. Synonyms Stadway Pippin, Walsgrove Blenheim as in our aka. Season dessert or culinary, November to March. Not the separate 'New Bess Pool' entry (line 4111).

bismarck.heading: BISMARK
bismarck.note: Tasmanian/Australian Bismark; Bunyard says it must not be confused with the German Bismark of 1877.

blenheim-orange.heading: BLENHEIM ORANGE
blenheim-orange.flavour: Flesh, crisp, yellow, sub-acid, with a characteristic flavour.
blenheim-orange.quality: One of the best all round apples grown, cooking excellently, and of fine quality and texture for dessert.
blenheim-orange.storage: Culinary or dessert, November to January
blenheim-orange.note: Bunyard keeps a separate Woodstock Pippin entry (line 6040) which he says is distinct, though his index also has 'Woodstock Pippin (error) : see Blenheim Orange'.

blue-pearmain.heading: BLUE PEARMAIN
blue-pearmain.flavour: Flesh, tender, yellow, rather dry, highly aromatic and sweet.
blue-pearmain.quality: A hardy variety worthy of further trial.
blue-pearmain.storage: Culinary or dessert, January to March
blue-pearmain.climate: It does well in Western Counties.

roxbury-russet.heading: BOSTON RUSSET
roxbury-russet.flavour: Flesh, firm, juicy, greenish, of excellent flavour
roxbury-russet.note: Bunyard: 'The correct name is Roxbury Russet.' Also says Reinette de Canada Grise is often wrongly called Boston Russet.

bow-hill-pippin.heading: BOW HILL PIPPIN
bow-hill-pippin.flavour: Flesh, firm, juicy, very yellow, good Blenheim flavour.
bow-hill-pippin.quality: A very good winter fruit of Blenheim character.
bow-hill-pippin.note: Introduced by the author's firm about 1893.

braddick-nonpareil.heading: BRADDICK'S NONPAREIL
braddick-nonpareil.quality: An apple of first class quality.
braddick-nonpareil.note: Synonym Ditton Pippin as in our aka.

bramleys-seedling.heading: BRAMLEY'S SEEDLING
bramleys-seedling.flavour: Flesh firm, juicy, pale yellow, acid.
bramleys-seedling.quality: This is the most popular and profitable of cooking apples
bramleys-seedling.climate: ironclad in constitution, growing wherever apples will grow.

calville-blanc-dhiver.heading: CALVILLE BLANCHE D'HIVER
calville-blanc-dhiver.flavour: Flesh, melting, pale yellow, aromatic. Of delicate flavour and remarkably melting texture
calville-blanc-dhiver.storage: Culinary or dessert, January to April
calville-blanc-dhiver.climate: Should be grown under glass or on a wall. Mr. Leake, of Wisbech, finds this to do excellently in his soil, which is almost free from lime.
calville-blanc-dhiver.note: Synonym White Calville listed. Growth weak, infertile.

calville-rouge-dhiver.heading: CALVILLE ROUGE D'HIVER
calville-rouge-dhiver.flavour: Flesh, crisp, white with occasional red touches, juicy, sub-acid.

catshead.heading: CATSHEAD
catshead.note: Superseded by others such as Lord Derby.

charles-ross.heading: CHARLES ROSS
charles-ross.flavour: Flesh, tender, short texture, fairly juicy, quite sweet, pleasant flavour.
charles-ross.quality: It is becoming a popular market apple
charles-ross.storage: Culinary or dessert, October to December
charles-ross.climate: does extremely well on thin soils on chalk.

chelmsford-wonder.heading: CHELMSFORD WONDER
chelmsford-wonder.flavour: Flesh, crisp and breaking, flavour, acid.
chelmsford-wonder.quality: A very useful fruit of the Wellington style in flesh
chelmsford-wonder.storage: it keeps crisp to a very late season.

christmas-pearmain.heading: CHRISTMAS PEARMAIN
christmas-pearmain.quality: This fruit is valuable for small gardens on account of its tree cropping powers.
christmas-pearmain.note: Introduced by the author's firm, G. Bunyard & Co., in 1895.

claygate-pearmain.heading: CLAYGATE PEARMAIN
claygate-pearmain.flavour: Flesh, crisp, ... juicy and of excellent flavour.
claygate-pearmain.quality: This is one of the best late dessert apples and is of the highest quality.
claygate-pearmain.note: Heading printed with a comma (missed by the candidate script). Synonym Ribston Pearmain as in our aka.

cockle-pippin.heading: COCKLE'S PIPPIN
cockle-pippin.climate: Of excellent flavour in warm seasons.
cockle-pippin.note: Synonym Pilot Russet as in our aka; Bunyard says distinct from Nutmeg Pippin. Season dessert, December to March.

colonel-vaughan.heading: COLONEL VAUGHAN
colonel-vaughan.flavour: Flesh, nearly white, firm, very juicy and sweet, often stained with a little red.
colonel-vaughan.quality: It crops so well and is so useful for small gardens that it seems a pity that it is almost forgotten in these days.
colonel-vaughan.storage: Culinary or dessert, November to January

cornish-aromatic.heading: CORNISH AROMATIC
cornish-aromatic.quality: This apple is of the highest quality, and appearance.

cornish-gilliflower.heading: CORNISH GILLYFLOWER
cornish-gilliflower.flavour: Flesh, firm, pale yellow, very richly flavoured.
cornish-gilliflower.climate: requires good treatment and a warm climate.
cornish-gilliflower.note: Probably not the July flower of Evelyn.

court-pendu-plat.heading: COURT PENDU PLAT
court-pendu-plat.climate: its late flowering habit often enabling it to escape early frosts. One of the best for a heavy clay soil.
court-pendu-plat.note: Synonyms Wise Apple, Garnons, Wollaton Pippin.

coxs-orange-pippin.heading: COX'S ORANGE
coxs-orange-pippin.flavour: Flesh, tender, yellow, juicy and of the highest flavour.
coxs-orange-pippin.quality: Generally considered to be the richest flavoured of English Apples.

coxs-pomona.heading: COX'S POMONA
coxs-pomona.storage: Dessert or culinary, October to December

crawley-beauty.heading: CRAWLEY BEAUTY
crawley-beauty.flavour: Flesh, firm, greenish-white, acid, good flavour when cooked.
crawley-beauty.quality: This promises to be a very useful variety, flowering very late.

crimson-bramley.heading: CRIMSON BRAMLEY
crimson-bramley.note: Short entry: a bud sport of Bramley's Seedling differing only in red colour; see the Bramley entry for flavour.

darcy-spice.heading: D'ARCY SPICE
darcy-spice.climate: but not often found thriving out of East Anglia.
darcy-spice.note: Synonyms Baddow Pippin, Essex Spice, Spring Ribston.

red-delicious.heading: DELICIOUS
red-delicious.flavour: Flesh, firm, yellow, juicy and highly flavoured.
red-delicious.quality: likely to prove a valuable fruit for Great Britain.
red-delicious.climate: Extremely hardy in its native country
red-delicious.note: The original Hiatt Delicious (Peru, Iowa, c.1880), introduced to England about 1912.

devonshire-quarrenden.heading: DEVONSHIRE QUARRENDEN
devonshire-quarrenden.flavour: Flesh, crisp, greenish, aromatic. Of most distinct and refreshing flavour

domino.heading: DOMINO
domino.quality: A useful fruit of the Codlin type.

duchesss-favourite.heading: DUCHESS' FAVOURITE
duchesss-favourite.flavour: Flesh, crisp, yellow, brisk and pleasant, often tinged with red.
duchesss-favourite.quality: This apple is attractive in appearance and largely grown for market use.

duchess-of-oldenburg.heading: DUCHESS OF OLDENBURG
duchess-of-oldenburg.quality: Of most attractive appearance, and a refreshing summer fruit.
duchess-of-oldenburg.storage: Culinary or dessert, August to September

duke-of-devonshire.heading: DUKE OF DEVONSHIRE
duke-of-devonshire.flavour: Flesh, firm, pale greenish-yellow, good flavour, rather dry.
duke-of-devonshire.quality: It is quite indispensable for late use.

dumelows-seedling.heading: DUMELOW'S SEEDLING
dumelows-seedling.quality: One of the best of cooking apples for those who like a brisk acidity.
dumelows-seedling.note: Heading OCR 'DUMMELOUS'. Synonyms Duke of Wellington, Normanton Wonder.

early-victoria.heading: EMNETH EARLY
early-victoria.quality: The best of the early codlins for crop, vigour, and appearance.
early-victoria.note: Heading gives (Early Victoria). Flesh is greenish-white (omitted from quote: OCR line-break hyphen defeats the validator).

easter-orange.heading: EASTER ORANGE
easter-orange.flavour: Flesh, firm, yellow, moderately juicy and of good flavour.
easter-orange.quality: A fruit of attractive appearance and good flavour for late winter and spring use.

ecklinville.heading: ECKLINVILLE
ecklinville.climate: Rather apt to canker in some soils.

edward-vii.heading: EDWARD VII
edward-vii.flavour: Flesh, extremely firm, yellow, acid, juicy.
edward-vii.quality: A valuable fruit, which should be more widely cultivated.

egremont-russet.heading: EGREMONT RUSSET
egremont-russet.flavour: Flesh, firm, greenish yellow, of very distinct and good flavour.
egremont-russet.quality: A delicious fruit, especially suited for garden use.

ellisons-orange.heading: ELLISON'S ORANGE
ellisons-orange.flavour: Flesh, tender, markedly yellow, of fair flavour.
ellisons-orange.quality: is of good flavour for a short period.
ellisons-orange.note: Bunyard says nothing of aniseed; only 'of good flavour for a short period'.

emperor-alexander.heading: EMPEROR ALEXANDER
emperor-alexander.quality: Valued chiefly on the exhibition table.
emperor-alexander.storage: Culinary or dessert, September to November

gascoynes-scarlet.heading: GASCOYNE'S SCARLET
gascoynes-scarlet.flavour: Flesh, loose, pale with red stainings; pleasant balsamic flavour.
gascoynes-scarlet.quality: now rarely grown, except for decorative purposes.
gascoynes-scarlet.note: Introduced by the author's firm in 1871.

gladstone.heading: GLADSTONE
gladstone.quality: Much grown for market purposes, and a valuable early sort.

golden-knob.heading: GOLDEN KNOB
golden-knob.flavour: Flesh, firm, greenish-yellow, sub-acid, good flavour.
golden-knob.quality: Still grown in Kentish orchards; of distinct flavour.

golden-noble.heading: GOLDEN NOBLE
golden-noble.flavour: Flesh, tender, yellow, acid. Cooks frothily and of golden colour.
golden-noble.quality: One of the very best cooking apples for colour and flavour.

golden-spire.heading: GOLDEN SPIRE
golden-spire.flavour: Flesh, pale yellow, juicy, soft, slightly flavoured.
golden-spire.quality: Its regular cropping and neat habit make it a fruit highly recommendable for small gardens.
golden-spire.note: Bunyard's 'slightly flavoured' sits oddly with our sharp/astringent tags but does not mention acidity.

gravenstein.heading: GRAVENSTEIN
gravenstein.flavour: Flesh, crisp, yellowish-white, extremely juicy, of most distinct flavour. Its fragrant aroma and digestible flesh make it deserving of wider cultivation.
gravenstein.storage: It has the unusual quality of ripening on the tree and yet keeping for several months.
gravenstein.note: A redder bud-sport form also noted.

grenadier.heading: GRENADIER
grenadier.quality: A very valuable cooking apple for August
grenadier.note: No flesh description; 'Cooks to a froth.' Often confused with Gold Medal.

hambledon-deux-ans.heading: HAMBLEDON DEUX ANS
hambledon-deux-ans.flavour: Flesh, dry, hard, yellow, a little sweet.
hambledon-deux-ans.storage: Culinary, January to August, A good late keeper.
hambledon-deux-ans.note: Synonyms Green Blenheim, Stone Blenheim, Deux Ans, Yorkshire Queen.

hawthornden.heading: HAWTHORNDEN
hawthornden.quality: One of the best cooking sorts

herrings-pippin.heading: HERRING'S PIPPIN
herrings-pippin.flavour: Flesh, pale yellow, tender, with a spicy aromatic flavour.
herrings-pippin.quality: Mr. Pearson who thinks very highly of this variety.
herrings-pippin.note: Bunyard had not grown it; described from fruit sent by Mr. Pearson.

james-grieve.heading: JAMES GRIEVE
james-grieve.flavour: Flesh, tender, very juicy, yellow, of excellent flavour.
james-grieve.quality: A most excellent fruit quite the best of its season
james-grieve.climate: its faults in the South are liability to rot and to fall prematurely.

kentish-fillbasket.heading: KENTISH FILL BASKET
kentish-fillbasket.quality: An old and good apple, now seldom grown.
kentish-fillbasket.note: Synonyms Lady de Grey's, Potter's Large as in our aka.

kerry-pippin.heading: KERRY PIPPIN
kerry-pippin.flavour: Flesh, very crisp, yellow, aromatic, brisk and juicy.
kerry-pippin.quality: A good fruit of the sub-acid type.

keswick-codlin.heading: KESWICK CODLIN
keswick-codlin.quality: Still appreciated for culinary use and its reliable cropping habits.

king-of-the-pippins.heading: KING OF THE PIPPINS
king-of-the-pippins.flavour: Flesh, creamy-yellow, firm, juicy with a distinct slightly bitter flavour.
king-of-the-pippins.note: Bunyard calls its history with the French Reine des Reinettes 'a tangle'; this is Hogg's Golden Winter Pearmain (our aka).

tompkins-king.heading: KING OF TOMKINS COUNTY
tompkins-king.flavour: Flesh, crisp, rather dry, tender, markedly yellow, sweet and of excellent flavour, slightly fragrant.
tompkins-king.climate: This I have seen equal to American samples from a Sandstone soil.
tompkins-king.note: Synonyms King, Winter King. Bunyard gives origin New Jersey before 1800.

lady-henniker.heading: LADY HENNIKER
lady-henniker.quality: A good old sort still worth growing.

lady-sudeley.heading: LADY SUDELEY
lady-sudeley.flavour: Flesh, yellow, tender, very juicy, of delicious flavour.
lady-sudeley.note: Raised by Mr. Jacobs of Petworth (cf. our aka Jacob's Strawberry); introduced by the author's firm in 1885. A paler russet sport exists.

landsberger-reinette.heading: LANDSBERGER REINETTE
landsberger-reinette.climate: It is said to be very firmly attached to the tree, thus withstanding autumnal gales.

lanes-prince-albert.heading: LANE'S PRINCE ALBERT
lanes-prince-albert.quality: Perhaps the most reliable cropper of all cooking apples.

lemon-pippin.heading: LEMON PIPPIN
lemon-pippin.quality: An old sort, now little grown.
lemon-pippin.note: Synonym Quince. Bunyard notes the name has also been applied to other apples.

lodgemore-nonpareil.heading: LODGEMORE NONPAREIL
lodgemore-nonpareil.flavour: Flesh, crisp, greenish, sweet, juicy, and well flavoured.
lodgemore-nonpareil.quality: An excellent old sort, now almost out of cultivation.

london-pippin.heading: LONDON PIPPIN
london-pippin.quality: A valuable late fruit little cultivated
london-pippin.storage: Culinary, till March. Keeps without shrivelling
london-pippin.note: Synonym Five Crown Pippin; much grown in Australia and exported to Britain.

lord-derby.heading: LORD DERBY
lord-derby.flavour: Flesh, firm, pale yellow, sub-acid. Cooks a deep golden red.
lord-derby.quality: One of the most appreciated sorts for market purposes, as it is an almost certain annual cropper.

lord-grosvenor.heading: LORD GROSVENOR
lord-grosvenor.flavour: Flesh, white, juicy, acid, cooking excellently.
lord-grosvenor.quality: One of the most prolific of all apples
lord-grosvenor.climate: it does well on dry soil.

lord-hindlip.heading: LORD HINDLIP
lord-hindlip.flavour: Flesh, crisp, white, sub-acid, juicy, and pleasantly flavoured.
lord-hindlip.quality: Of very good quality and a good cropper

lord-suffield.heading: LORD SUFFIELD
lord-suffield.note: Synonyms Lady Suffield, Livesay's Imperial. Cankers badly and apt to rot on the tree.

mcintosh-red.heading: MACKINTOSH RED
mcintosh-red.flavour: Flesh, greenish white, firm, slightly sweet, juicy.
mcintosh-red.quality: has not yet been sufficiently tested at Allington to decide upon its value for this country.
mcintosh-red.storage: Culinary or dessert, October to December
mcintosh-red.note: Spelled Mackintosh; named after Allan Mackintosh, Ontario.

maidstone-favourite.heading: MAIDSTONE FAVOURITE
maidstone-favourite.flavour: Flesh, creamy white, fine grained, sweet and juicy, very firm. One of the most beautiful apples of Autumn, a little lacking in flavour
maidstone-favourite.quality: One of the most beautiful apples of Autumn, a little lacking in flavour but very promising for market culture
maidstone-favourite.note: Raised by the author's firm from a seed of Emperor Alexander. Season dessert, end-August to September.

manks-codlin.heading: MANK'S CODLIN
manks-codlin.quality: one of the best cooking apples there.
manks-codlin.climate: It is still much grown in the North of England and is one of the best cooking apples there.
manks-codlin.note: Synonyms Belmont, Eve, Irish Codlin, Pitcher.

margil.heading: MARGIL
margil.note: Synonyms Reinette Musquee, Muskat Reinette, Small Ribston.

mere-de-menage.heading: MERE DE MENAGE
mere-de-menage.storage: A useful kitchen fruit, keeping well.
mere-de-menage.note: Bunyard: 'not the Mere de Menage of France'; grown in Belgium as Queen Emma; much grown in East Anglia. He also says Flanders Pippin (in our aka) is quite distinct (own entry, line 2483).

millers-seedling.heading: MILLER'S SEEDLING
millers-seedling.quality: A very sweet fruit, appreciated as a market variety in some districts.

american-mother.heading: MOTHER
american-mother.flavour: Flesh, soft and juicy, very sweet, yellow or slightly green of distinct flavour, resembling Peardrops.
american-mother.storage: which often keeps good till mid January.
american-mother.note: Bunyard notes Hogg prefixed 'American' to distinguish it from other Mothers.

newton-wonder.heading: NEWTON WONDER
newton-wonder.flavour: Flesh, crisp, juicy, yellow, acid; cooks excellently.
newton-wonder.quality: One of the best half-dozen cooking apples.
newton-wonder.storage: Culinary, till March. Quite a welcome dessert fruit in March.

newtown-pippin.heading: NEWTOWN PIPPIN
newtown-pippin.flavour: Flesh, very crisp, yellowish-green, of rich pineapple flavour.
newtown-pippin.climate: This apple does not attain to the same flavour in this country as in America, even under the most favourable conditions.
newtown-pippin.note: Synonym Albemarle. Fertility poor in England; a green form considered distinct.

nonpareil.heading: NONPAREIL
nonpareil.quality: This fruit is worthy of all commendation.

norfolk-beauty.heading: NORFOLK BEAUTY
norfolk-beauty.quality: A very excellent fruit worthy of extended cultivation

norfolk-beefing.heading: NORFOLK BEEFING
norfolk-beefing.storage: Culinary, till April. A useful late fruit, keeping plump till the end.

northern-spy.heading: NORTHERN SPY
northern-spy.flavour: Flesh, loose, juicy, greenish-yellow, of good flavour.
northern-spy.climate: This apple only does well in England in very favourable years.

orleans-reinette.heading: ORLEAN'S REINETTE
orleans-reinette.flavour: Flesh, yellow, very crisp, sweet, juicy and of the highest flavour intermediate between Blenheim Orange and Ribston Pippin.
orleans-reinette.quality: This magnificent fruit cannot be too highly recommended.
orleans-reinette.note: Bunyard's firm sold it as Winter Ribston (our aka) before the real name was found; he finds the flavour much better than Blenheim's.

arbroath-pippin.heading: OSLIN
arbroath-pippin.note: Synonyms Arbroath Pippin, Burr Knot, Mother, Original Pippin, Summer Oslin. (Bunyard's separate BURR KNOT entry is a different apple.)

peasgoods-nonsuch.heading: PEASGOOD'S NONSUCH
peasgoods-nonsuch.flavour: Flesh, tender, yellowish, of pleasant flavour and cooks frothily.
peasgoods-nonsuch.quality: One of the most beautiful fruits grown; first rate for cooking.
peasgoods-nonsuch.storage: Culinary and exhibition, September to November
peasgoods-nonsuch.note: Heading OCR 'PEASGOGD'S' (missed by the candidate script). Rather liable to canker.

pitmaston-pine-apple.heading: PITMASTON PINE APPLE
pitmaston-pine-apple.flavour: Flesh, yellow, firm, juicy with a most deliciously scented and honeyed flavour.
pitmaston-pine-apple.quality: its distinct and delicious flavour should give it a place in the gardens of connoisseurs.
pitmaston-pine-apple.note: Bunyard says raised from the Old Golden Pippin by Mr. White of Witley, not by Mr. Williams of Pitmaston as Hogg says. No pineapple word in this entry.

pomme-gris.heading: POMME GRISE
pomme-gris.note: Origin 'probably Canadian', introduced to England 1794; synonyms Gray Apple, Leather Coat of Turic, Pomme de Cuir.

leathercoat-russet.heading: ROYAL RUSSET
leathercoat-russet.quality: One of the best of its class.
leathercoat-russet.note: Listed as 'Leather Coat (of some)'; index 'Leather Coat : see Royal Russet'; first recorded 1597 as in our record. Bunyard calls Reinette de Canada Grise an erroneous synonym of it.

reverend-w-wilks.heading: REV. W. WILKS
reverend-w-wilks.flavour: Flesh, tender, white, sub-acid, cooks frothily, pale yellow.
reverend-w-wilks.quality: A very large and promising fruit, of excellent cooking qualities.
reverend-w-wilks.note: Peasgood Nonsuch x Ribston, raised by Veitch.

rhode-island-greening.heading: RHODE ISLAND GREENING
rhode-island-greening.flavour: Flesh, crisp, very juicy, pale yellow, spicy flavour.
rhode-island-greening.quality: A useful late fruit of the Newtown Pippin style.
rhode-island-greening.storage: Quite good for dessert in March and April when well ripened.

ribston-pippin.heading: RIBSTON PIPPIN
ribston-pippin.quality: One of the richest flavoured apples when well ripened.

rome-beauty.heading: ROME BEAUTY
rome-beauty.flavour: Flesh, palest yellow, crisp, juicy, a little sweet, not any marked flavour.

rosemary-russet.heading: ROSEMARY RUSSET
rosemary-russet.flavour: Flesh, crisp, yellow, very rich and brisk.
rosemary-russet.quality: Quite the best of late winter apples.

ross-nonpareil.heading: ROSS NONPAREIL
ross-nonpareil.flavour: Flesh, tender, greenish, aromatic, strongly scented.
ross-nonpareil.quality: A first rate garden fruit, as good in flavour as it is attractive in appearance.
ross-nonpareil.note: Heading OCR 'RpSS' (found by own search). Irish, introduced to England 1820. No fennel/anise word here.

royal-jubilee.heading: ROYAL JUBILEE
royal-jubilee.flavour: Flesh, firm, yellow, sub-acid: cooks well.
royal-jubilee.quality: Valuable for its late flowering and regular cropping habits.
royal-jubilee.note: Raised by John Graham of Hounslow; introduced by the author's firm 1893.

signe-tillisch.heading: SIGNE TILLISCH
signe-tillisch.flavour: Flesh, white, moderately firm, a little sweet.

sops-in-wine.heading: SOPS IN WINE
sops-in-wine.flavour: Flesh, tender, white, much stained with red; flavourless.
sops-in-wine.quality: It is of no particular merit.
sops-in-wine.note: Bunyard: many red-fleshed apples bear this name; he believes this is the Old English one.

st-edmunds-pippin.heading: ST. EDMUND'S PIPPIN
st-edmunds-pippin.flavour: Flesh, pale yellow, very juicy and fine flavoured.

stirling-castle.heading: STIRLING CASTLE
stirling-castle.quality: A valuable fruit, remarkable for its fertility

sturmer-pippin.heading: STURMER PIPPIN
sturmer-pippin.flavour: Flesh, crisp, juicy, greenish, brisk and pleasantly flavoured.
sturmer-pippin.quality: An indispensable fruit for late use.
sturmer-pippin.storage: Dessert, till May. It should be left on the tree as late as possible.
sturmer-pippin.climate: It does well on either light or heavy soils.

tom-putt.heading: TOM PUTT
tom-putt.flavour: Flesh, crisp, acid, greenish white, cooking excellently.
tom-putt.quality: A great favourite in the Western counties.
tom-putt.note: Synonym Tom Potter. Bunyard thinks the fruit Hogg described is not the true variety.

tower-of-glamis.heading: TOWER OF GLAMIS
tower-of-glamis.note: Heading OCR 'TOWAR'. Synonyms Carse o'Gowrie, Dunster Codlin. Recognised by its unusual heaviness.

transparente-de-croncels.heading: TRANSPARENT DE CRONCELS
transparente-de-croncels.flavour: Flesh, pale yellow, crisp, tender, juicy, with a distinct flavour.
transparente-de-croncels.storage: Culinary or dessert, October to December
transparente-de-croncels.climate: One of the few apples in France which was quite uninjured by the great frost of 1879.

twenty-ounce.heading: TWENTY OUNCE
twenty-ounce.flavour: Flesh, loose, pale yellow, sub-acid, fairly juicy.
twenty-ounce.quality: Of value only for exhibition and pot culture.

warners-king.heading: WARNER'S KING
warners-king.note: Synonyms D. T. Fish, King, Killick's Apple, Weavering. Rather liable to canker.

wealthy.heading: WEALTHY
wealthy.flavour: Flesh, white, often slightly stained with red, loose grained, juicy, very sweet, with a pleasant strawberry flavour.
wealthy.quality: This apple is almost worth growing for its appearance alone
wealthy.note: Bunyard finds it rather too soft for market use.

white-transparent.heading: WHITE TRANSPARENT
white-transparent.flavour: Flesh, greenish-white, crisp, acid. A delicious summer fruit, brisk and digestible.

william-crump.heading: WILLIAM CRUMP
william-crump.flavour: Flesh, rather firm, greenish-yellow, of good flavour.
william-crump.quality: A good addition to the late dessert sorts.

winter-banana.heading: WINTER BANANA
winter-banana.flavour: Flesh, pale yellow, a little coarse grained, juicy, aromatic.
winter-banana.quality: the quality and fertility which it will attain in this country are somewhat doubtful.
winter-banana.note: No banana word in this entry.

winter-pearmain.heading: WINTER QUEENING
winter-pearmain.note: Winter Queening = Winter Quoining (our aka), an old Sussex variety; index 'Sussex Ducks Bill : see Winter Queening', but Bunyard fancies Sussex Duck's Bill is really distinct. Our record mixes these names, hence probable.

worcester-pearmain.heading: WORCESTER PEARMAIN
worcester-pearmain.flavour: Flesh, crisp, greenish, very sweet, with a pleasant strawberry flavour.
worcester-pearmain.quality: The flavour of this fruit is greatly underrated by many, as it is usually gathered and eaten far before it is ripe.

yellow-ingestrie.heading: YELLOW INGESTRIE
yellow-ingestrie.note: Bunyard says Summer Golden Pippin (in our aka) is distinct and has its own entry.

akero.heading: AKERO
akero.quality: This is now rarely grown, but is of interest only from its remarkable coloration.
akero.note: Book's synonyms Akera, Okera; 'Origin, probably Swedish'. Says nothing about taste.

alfriston.heading: ALFRISTON
alfriston.flavour: Flesh, crisp, pale yellow, sub-acid. This apple cooks a tender, golden brown with a delicious pear-like flavour.
alfriston.note: Synonyms Shepherd's Pippin, Shepherd's Seedling as in our aka; raised by Mr. Shepherd at Alfriston, Sussex. The pear-like flavour is of the cooked apple.

ard-cairn-russet.heading: ARD CAIRN RUSSET
ard-cairn-russet.flavour: Flesh, yellow, firm, good russet flavour.
ard-cairn-russet.note: An old Irish variety introduced by Hartland of Ard Cairn, Co. Cork.

baumanns-reinette.heading: BAUMANN'S REINETTE
baumanns-reinette.flavour: Flesh, white, crisp, juicy, slightly aromatic.
baumanns-reinette.quality: A remarkable cropper but of poor quality.
baumanns-reinette.storage: Culinary or dessert, December to January
baumanns-reinette.note: Synonyms Couronne des Dames, Reinette de Bolwyller as in our aka; raised probably by Van Mons.

baxters-pearmain.heading: BAXTER'S PEARMAIN
baxters-pearmain.flavour: Flesh, yellowish, tender, pleasantly acid. It is rather too acid for some palates.
baxters-pearmain.storage: Dessert or culinary, December to February
baxters-pearmain.note: A Norfolk variety introduced by G. Lindley in 1821.

bietigheimer.heading: BIETIGHEIMER
bietigheimer.flavour: Flesh, firm, greenish-white, sweet but with no aroma.
bietigheimer.note: Bunyard treats Bietigheimer as a synonym of Rother Stettiner (Rouge de Stettin, 'more than twenty-five' synonyms) and says that is the correct name; the large crimson culinary fruit fits our record, but the Stettiner confusion makes the identity uncertain. His 'sweet' sits awkwardly with our sharp tag.

edelborsdorfer.heading: BORSDORFER
edelborsdorfer.flavour: Flesh, firm, juicy, pale yellow, poor flavour.
edelborsdorfer.quality: A worthless fruit in this country, except in very warm seasons.
edelborsdorfer.climate: A worthless fruit in this country, except in very warm seasons.
edelborsdorfer.note: Book gives G. Edelborsdorfer; German, recorded by Cordus in 1561; imported for Queen Charlotte.

fenouillet-gris.heading: CARAWAY RUSSET
fenouillet-gris.quality: A reliable sort still grown in old orchards.
fenouillet-gris.note: Bunyard: 'The correct name is Fenouillet Gris'; Leroy takes it for the Epice d'Hiver of Olivier de Serres. No mention of aniseed in the flesh description despite the name.

cellini.heading: CELLINI
cellini.flavour: Flesh, tender white, sub-acid, with curious balsamic flavour. Regular cropping is its chief recommendation, but the curious flavour appeals to some.
cellini.quality: Regular cropping is its chief recommendation
cellini.note: Synonym Phillips' Seedling; raised by Leonard Phillips, Vauxhall, about 1828. 'Balsamic' is not in our tag list.

dutch-mignonne.heading: DUTCH MIGNONNE
dutch-mignonne.quality: A most useful, fertile fruit. Considered by many to be worthy of dessert use late in the season.
dutch-mignonne.note: F. Reinette de Caux; G. Grosser Casseler Reinette; Paternoster - all in our aka. Bunyard: 'Grosser Casseler Reinette is the original name'.

frogmore-prolific.heading: FROGMORE PROLIFIC
frogmore-prolific.note: Raised in the Royal Gardens at Frogmore by Mr. Ingram.

gloria-mundi.heading: GLORIA MUNDI
gloria-mundi.flavour: Flesh, tender, white, sub-acid. It cooks a brown colour, but is very sweet and rich.
gloria-mundi.quality: Too uncertain a cropper in most parts.
gloria-mundi.note: Synonyms Monstrous Pippin, Ox Apple, Mammoth as in our aka; first recorded in America in 1804.

golden-harvey.heading: GOLDEN HARVEY
golden-harvey.flavour: Flesh, firm, yellow, very sweet and rich.
golden-harvey.quality: One of the good old sorts which have been neglected.
golden-harvey.note: Synonyms Brandy Apple, Round Russet Harvey as in our aka; English, known early in the seventeenth century.

histon-favourite.heading: HISTON FAVOURITE
histon-favourite.flavour: Flesh, soft, pale yellow, juicy, slight aromatic flavour.
histon-favourite.quality: A nice fruit, but rather too small with me.
histon-favourite.storage: Dessert or cooking, November to December
histon-favourite.note: Book's synonym Oliver's Seedling; raised at Histon by John Chivers (our aka Chivers' Seedling).

kandil-sinap.heading: KANDIL SINAP
kandil-sinap.flavour: Flesh, white, crisp, tender, juicy, and slight flavour.
kandil-sinap.quality: It is one of the most popular market varieties in the Crimea.
kandil-sinap.note: F. Candile Sinope; 'This Russian fruit is remarkable for its elongated barrel shape'.

manningtons-pearmain.heading: MANNINGTON'S PEARMAIN
manningtons-pearmain.flavour: Flesh, crisp, yellow, fair flavour. The flavour of this variety is only fair
manningtons-pearmain.quality: as there are so many better at this season I consider it not worth growing.

melon.heading: MELON
melon.flavour: Flesh, pale yellow, tender, juicy, somewhat aromatic.
melon.quality: A good useful late fruit now seldom met with.
melon.note: The New York Melon (Norton's Melon) from the Heman Chapin orchard, East Bloomfield, introduced by Ellwanger & Barry in 1845 - same apple as ours despite the homonym risk.

nanny.heading: NANNY
nanny.flavour: Flesh, tender, greenish yellow, a little sweet, but of no remarkable flavour.
nanny.note: A Sussex apple. Bunyard has a separate SEPTEMBER BEAUTY (line 5293, Laxton c.1885), so our aka September Beauty is probably a different apple.

ontario.heading: ONTARIO
ontario.flavour: Flesh, crisp, juicy, pale yellow, sub-acid.
ontario.quality: An excellent late variety, worthy of extended cultivation.
ontario.storage: It does not shrivel when kept long.
ontario.note: Wagener x Northern Spy by Charles Arnold, Ontario, before 1874.

potts-seedling.heading: POTTS' SEEDLING
potts-seedling.quality: A useful kitchen fruit. Most valuable for small gardens.
potts-seedling.note: Synonyms Dean's Codlin, Holland Pippin (the latter is NOT our holland-pippin). Raised at Ashton-under-Lyne, dates from 1849.

reinette-du-canada.heading: REINETTE DU CANADA
reinette-du-canada.flavour: Flesh, firm, pale yellow, of rich flavour.
reinette-du-canada.climate: Excellent in warm seasons. Very subject to canker.
reinette-du-canada.note: G. Pariser Rambour Reinette; 'some forty-eight synonyms'; known in France before 1771.

reinette-rouge-etoilee.heading: REINETTE ROUGE ETOILEE
reinette-rouge-etoilee.flavour: Flesh, firm, juicy, pale yellow with suffused red below skin, sub-acid, of slight strawberry flavour.
reinette-rouge-etoilee.quality: Of fair quality and most attractive in appearance.
reinette-rouge-etoilee.note: Synonyms Early Red Calville, Reinette Etoilee as in our aka; 'the Early Red Calville of Hogg'.

renown.heading: RENOWN
renown.flavour: Flesh, pale yellow, firm, of pleasant flavour.
renown.storage: Dessert or culinary, October to November
renown.note: Raised by Charles Ross from the same cross as Charles Ross; Gard. Chron. 1908.

star-of-devon.heading: STAR OF DEVON
star-of-devon.flavour: Flesh, soft, nearly white, of poor flavour.
star-of-devon.quality: Up to the present no particular merit has been discovered.
star-of-devon.note: Raised by J. Garland, Broad Clyst, Devon; introduced 1905 by George Pyne, Topsham.

upton-pyne.heading: UPTON PYNE
upton-pyne.flavour: Flesh, firm, white, juicy, of brisk pine flavour.
upton-pyne.quality: Of very distinct flavour and likely to become popular.
upton-pyne.note: Raised by Mr. Pyne of Topsham, introduced in 1910.

venus-pippin.heading: VENUS PIPPIN
venus-pippin.flavour: Flesh, tender, pale yellow, juicy and refreshing flavour.
venus-pippin.quality: Rather too soft for market use and hardly worth retention.
venus-pippin.storage: Dessert or culinary, September to October
venus-pippin.note: Synonym Plumderity as in our aka; 'said to have been raised about 1800'.

wagener.heading: WAGENER
wagener.flavour: Flesh, firm, juicy, yellow, pleasantly flavoured.
wagener.quality: One of the best late varieties
wagener.note: G. Wageners Preis Apfel; raised in the garden of Abraham Wagener about 1796 at Dover, New York.

williams-favourite.heading: WILLIAM'S FAVOURITE
williams-favourite.quality: One of the best early dessert apples and well worthy of culture.
williams-favourite.note: Origin at Roxbury, U.S.A., about 1750. 'sott' is the OCR's misreading of 'soft' (left as printed so the quote validates).
